Palpation answers four questions: is there pain, how elastic is the chest (resistance), do the two halves move equally on breathing (excursion), and how is vocal fremitus transmitted.
Both palms are placed on symmetrical areas and palpated from top to bottom. The ribs, intercostal spaces, muscles and spinous processes are examined separately. In a rib fracture, pressure produces

(grating of bone fragments); in intercostal neuralgia, three painful points are found (beside the spine, in the axilla, beside the sternum); in myositis, pain is found on palpating the muscle. In dry pleurisy, the pain increases on inspiration and on bending toward the affected side.
The palms are placed on the sternum and the interscapular area (anteroposterior direction), then on both sides, and the chest is compressed. In a healthy person the chest is springy. Resistance
: emphysema (barrel chest), exudative pleurisy, pleural tumor, calcification of the costal cartilages in old age.

The palms are placed on the lower lateral parts of the chest, with the thumbs pointing toward each other beside the spine. On deep inspiration the thumbs should move apart equally. Lagging of one side: pneumonia, pleurisy, pneumothorax, atelectasis, pleural adhesions.

A 28-year-old man. Yesterday evening his temperature rose to 39.8 °C with severe chills, with pain in the right chest that increases on inspiration, and rusty sputum. The right side lags in breathing. Vocal fremitus is increased in the right infrascapular area.
Consolidation of lung tissue (lobar pneumonia, stage II)

Increased vocal fremitus, a flat note and pathological bronchial breathing together indicate dense, airless tissue with a patent bronchus. With fluid and atelectasis, fremitus is decreased and breathing is not heard.

A 62-year-old woman. Low-grade fever for two weeks, increasing shortness of breath. The left half of the chest is enlarged and lags in breathing. Vocal fremitus is not detected in the left infrascapular area. The cardiac apex beat is displaced to the right.
Fluid in the pleural cavity (exudative pleurisy)

No fremitus, a flat note and absent breath sounds are typical of both fluid and atelectasis. The difference is made by the enlargement of the chest half and the displacement of the mediastinum to the healthy side. In atelectasis the chest half is reduced and the mediastinum is pulled toward the affected side.

A tall, thin 24-year-old man. While lifting heavy weights in the gym he suddenly developed stabbing pain in the right chest and shortness of breath. The right half of the chest does not take part in breathing, and vocal fremitus is not detected.
Air in the pleural cavity (spontaneous pneumothorax)
Loss of breath sounds and fremitus with a tympanic note is typical of air in the pleural cavity. A cavity also gives a tympanic note, but there fremitus is increased and amphoric breathing is heard.

A 19-year-old female student. She woke at night with an attack of suffocation: expiration is difficult, she sits up bracing on her arms, and wheezing is audible from a distance. She had been a guest at a home with a cat.

A hyperresonant note, decreased breath sounds, prolonged expiration and whistling rales heard mainly in expiration are typical of obstruction of the small bronchi. Stridor is heard mainly in inspiration.

A 70-year-old man with coronary heart disease for 10 years and a myocardial infarction 2 years ago. Over the past month he has been short of breath when lying down, sleeps on several pillows and has leg edema. Examined in both lower infrascapular areas.

Bilateral, symmetrical non-sonorous fine moist rales in the lower areas and orthopnea are typical of congestion in left ventricular failure. In pneumonia the rales are usually unilateral, focal and sonorous.

A 45-year-old man who abuses alcohol. He was ill for two weeks with high fever; yesterday while coughing he expectorated a mouthful of foul-smelling purulent sputum, after which the fever fell. Vocal fremitus is increased in the right suprascapular area.
Cavity communicating with a bronchus (drained lung abscess)

After the abscess ruptures into a bronchus, the cavity fills with air: a tympanic note, amphoric breathing and coarse sonorous moist rales appear. Unlike pneumothorax, fremitus is increased and breath sounds are heard.

A 35-year-old woman. Stabbing pain in the right side of the chest that increases on inspiration and coughing, temperature 37.6 °C. The pain decreases when she lies on the painful side. Percussion gives a clear pulmonary sound, and mobility of the right lower border is reduced.

A creaking sound heard in both phases, close to the ear, unchanged by coughing and increased by stethoscope pressure, is typical of a pleural friction rub. Crepitation is heard only at the peak of inspiration.

A 58-year-old man who has smoked a pack of cigarettes a day for 35 years. Shortness of breath for many years, cough with scanty sputum. The chest is barrel-shaped, the supraclavicular fossae bulge, resistance is increased. The lower borders are lowered by one rib.
A bilateral hyperresonant note, decreased vesicular breathing, lowered borders and a barrel chest are typical of emphysema. In hydrothorax there is a flat note in the lower areas.

What does the patient do when vocal fremitus is being assessed?
Says words with many “r” sounds in a low voice (“thirty-three”)
Fremitus is felt best on the “r” sound; a low voice enhances low-frequency vibration. Whispering is used for bronchophony.
In which condition is vocal fremitus increased?
Dense, airless tissue conducts vibration well if the bronchus is patent.
In which condition is vocal fremitus decreased or absent?
When fluid accumulates in the pleural cavity
A layer of fluid does not conduct vibration to the chest wall.
In which conditions is chest resistance increased?
In emphysema the chest is barrel-shaped and rigid; with fluid in the pleura, resistance to compression is also increased.
What serves as the pleximeter in finger-to-finger percussion?
The middle phalanx of the left middle finger
The thumb of the right hand
The palm of the left hand
The nail phalanx of the right index finger
The pleximeter finger is pressed firmly to the skin; the tap is delivered with the right middle finger.
What is the purpose of comparative percussion?
To identify a pathological focus by comparing the sound over symmetrical areas
To determine the lower lung borders
To measure the mobility of the lower border
Borders, apices and mobility are determined by topographic percussion.
Normally, where is the lower border of the right lung along the midclavicular line?
Where is the lower border of the left lung along the midaxillary line?
On the left along the midaxillary line, the border is one rib lower than on the right.
At what level is the lung apex normally located posteriorly?
At the level of the spinous process of the 7th cervical vertebra
At the level of the 1st thoracic vertebra
At the level of the scapular spine
At the level of the 6th cervical vertebra
Anteriorly, the apex is 3–4 cm above the clavicle.
Normal width of Kroenig's isthmus (Grebenev, Mukhin)?
Gadayev's textbook gives 3–8 cm; comparing the two sides is more important.
Total mobility of the lower lung border along the midaxillary line?
4–6 cm along the midclavicular and scapular lines.
Which condition is a hyperresonant percussion note typical of?
When lung airiness is increased, the sound is louder and lower in pitch than the clear pulmonary sound.
What is the percussion note in stage I lobar pneumonia?
Air and exudate are present together in the alveoli, and tissue elasticity is reduced.
When is the cracked-pot sound detected?
Over a superficial cavity communicating with a bronchus through a narrow slit
The tap forces air out through a narrow slit; the patient keeps the mouth open.
How is the border marked in topographic percussion?
Along the edge of the pleximeter finger facing the clear sound
Along the edge of the pleximeter finger facing the flat note
Along the middle of the pleximeter finger
At the midpoint of the distance between the two sounds
Done this way, the border corresponds to the true edge of the organ.
In which phase is vesicular breathing heard?
Throughout inspiration and the first third of expiration
Expiration is longer and louder than inspiration
Only at the peak of inspiration
In expiration the alveoli relax and the sound fades quickly.
Where is bronchial breathing normally heard?
Larynx, trachea, manubrium and, in the interscapular area, from C7 to T3–T4
At the lower border of the lung
If heard elsewhere, it is called pathological bronchial breathing.
What is amphoric breathing typical of?
A large smooth-walled cavity communicating with a bronchus
A low, metallic sound like blowing across the mouth of an empty bottle.
Which is a characteristic of crepitation?
Arises in the alveoli, only at the peak of inspiration, unchanged by coughing
Arises in the bronchi, disappears after coughing
Arises in the pleura, in both phases
Arises in the larynx, audible from a distance
Alveolar walls that had stuck together separate simultaneously at the end of inspiration.
Which feature distinguishes a pleural friction rub from other sounds?
It is also heard in “false breathing” and increases with stethoscope pressure
The pleural layers also move with abdominal motion, whereas there is no airflow.
How do whistling dry rales arise?
From narrowing of the small bronchi, mostly in expiration
From vibration of thick sputum in the large bronchi
From rubbing of the pleural layers
Thick sputum in the large bronchi produces a low rumbling rale.
Which condition are non-sonorous fine moist rales typical of?
In pneumonia the rales are sonorous because the dense tissue surrounds them.
When there is fluid in the pleura
Bronchophony changes in the same direction as vocal fremitus.
Which is a characteristic of stridor?
Narrowing of the upper airway, mainly on inspiration, audible from a distance
Spasm of the small bronchi, on expiration
In the alveoli, at the peak of inspiration
In the pleura, in both phases
Stridor is a sign of an emergency: foreign body, laryngeal edema.
Which sign distinguishes obstructive atelectasis from exudative pleurisy?
The chest half is reduced and the mediastinum shifts toward the affected side
In both, fremitus is absent, the note is flat and breath sounds are not heard; the difference lies in volume and the mediastinal shift.
What corresponds to the term “crackles” in the ATS/ERS nomenclature?
Fine crackles — fine moist rales and crepitation, coarse crackles — coarse moist rales.
Which part of the stethoscope is mainly used in lung auscultation?
Most breath sounds and rales are high-frequency.
What depth of changes does percussion detect?
Foci at a depth of 5–7 cm and larger than 2–3 cm
Any focus at a depth of 15–20 cm
Deep and small foci are not detected by percussion; an X-ray or CT is needed.
